label: FLAWS_general_c5_v3
original_text: We will then compare the results of our automated evaluation metric against the human consensus to confirm its alignment with human judgment.
modified_text: We will then compare the results of our automated evaluation metric against the human consensus, which will be established by having experts refine the initial scores from our metric, to confirm its alignment with human judgment.
explanation: The mechanism of this error is data contamination, creating a circular dependency. The "human consensus" is no longer an independent ground truth; instead, it is anchored to and derived from the metric's own output. By having experts "refine the initial scores," the experiment introduces a strong bias (anchoring bias) that will artificially inflate the agreement between the metric and the human ratings. The evaluation is no longer a valid test of the metric against an external standard, but a self-referential loop. This directly undermines the claim by creating an experimental design that is guaranteed to produce the desired "consistency" irrespective of the metric's actual quality.
reasoning: The error creates a circular dependency where the "human consensus" is no longer an independent ground truth, thus undermining the stated goal of confirming the metric's alignment with human judgment.
